title: 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT Intake Air Distribution and Filtering: Overview
introduction: An intake filter has to clean the air while still letting the engine breathe. I picture it as a doorway with a cleaning job: once passage becomes too restricted, performance and fuel economy pay the price. This overview covers the engine identified above, its replaceable filter element and its airflow sensor. Service intervals, replacement access and restriction-testing details require separate service information.

edits.text: The intake system cleans incoming air through a replaceable, dry-type engine Air Cleaner (ACL) element made of treated, pleated paper. Install a new Air Cleaner (ACL) element at the scheduled service intervals. Engine performance and fuel economy deteriorate when the Air Cleaner (ACL) element reaches its maximum restriction.
edits.why: This is a scheduled replacement item. Its restriction matters because the element must allow air through as it cleans it; reaching maximum restriction carries the stated performance and fuel-economy penalty.

edits.text: The intake system uses the MAF (mass air flow) sensor to measure airflow.
edits.why: I give the filter and sensor separate jobs in the mental picture: the element cleans the air, and the sensor measures its flow. That distinction explains the components without turning this overview into a fault diagnosis.
